subject: Sticky KV cache + concurrency carveout request for Reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Leah Park <leah.park@evergreen.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre-team@evergreen.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity carveout: sticky KV cache + concurrent batch windows

Mateo —

Thanks for taking this. We've been seeing recurring queueing and tail-latency spikes during our nightly ingestion window when our batch job rehydrates long-lived KV caches. Even with our Reserved GPU pool we observe preemption and queued requests from our low-latency inference traffic.

Can Redwood provide an operational carveout or SLA amendment to ensure: 1) our pinned "sticky" KV cache workloads are not preempted by short-lived bursts during the 01:00-03:00 UTC batch window; and 2) a clear throughput/latency commitment for those pinned workloads (95th percentile tail guidance).

We're happy to accept constraints (e.g., fixed concurrency per reserved GPU, scheduled batch window, or fixed headroom reservation) as part of the carveout. Our procurement team would like a short written amendment we can attach to the PO.

I've attached a snapshot of our observed SLO violations for reference (evergreen-slo-snapshot-20270403.pdf).

Appreciate a proposed mitigation and timeline — we need to confirm by end of next week to meet our project launch.

Best,
Leah Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Evergreen Labs

---
(Attachment: evergreen-slo-snapshot-20270403.pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Leah Park <leah.park@evergreen.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre-team@evergreen.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity carveout: sticky KV cache + concurrent batch windows

Leah —

Thanks for the detail and the SLO snapshot, very helpful. We can support a scoped carveout for pinned KV cache workloads on Reserved GPU pools. Proposed approach (summary):

- Carveout window: scheduleable daily window (default 01:00-03:00 UTC) where batch rehydration runs with non-preemptible reservations.
- Isolation mechanism: a "sticky-KV" tenant label that pins KV shard processes to reserved GPUs; these slots will have queue-weight priority and be excluded from short-lived ephemeral preemption.
- Throughput / latency commitment: for pinned workloads we will guarantee a baseline throughput headroom (equivalent to 1.2x of your steady-state tokens/s observed across attached pool) and a 95th percentile response latency target no worse than 120ms under normal load inside the carveout.
- Operational constraints: carveout requires a static concurrency cap (configurable) per reserved GPU, and each carveout will be limited to the capacity you commit in the PO (we will map to N dedicated GPUs).
- Fallbacks: outside the carveout window, normal routing applies; if the pinned pool reaches saturation we'll provide automatic spillover routing to a lower-priority queue (with explicit throttling) rather than preempting pinned slots.

I'll prepare a short amendment doc you can attach to your PO and route to legal — sending a draft and internal alignment note shortly.

High level timeline: internal sign-off + ops configuration ~ 3 business days after mutual approval; DocuSign-ready amendment same day.

Does this sound like the right tradeoff for Evergreen? If so I'll loop in Diego and Naomi to get capacity mapping and a PO-friendly SLA clause drafted.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Action items:

Also confirm we can produce the 95th percentile latency metrics for an agreed baseline and whether 120ms is achievable for their current pool sizing.
- Lauren (Legal): I'll need a one-paragraph amendment that references "Reserved GPU carveout for pinned KV-cache workloads" and the operational constraints (window, static concurrency, capacity limit). Keep it high level — Evergreen will attach to procurement paperwork.
- Naomi (Product): please confirm this doesn't introduce global routing regressions and whether we should mark this as a product opt-in vs. customer-specific exception.

Target: internal sign-off by Wed EOD so we can get the amendment into DocuSign and meet EVG's timeline.

Thanks —
Mateo
